data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim that the preference is a 'non-rational, psychological commitment' contradicts Popper's explicit argument in 'Conjectures and Refutations' that preferring the better-corroborated theory is the only 'rational' course of action available, even if it lacks logical justification. Popper distinguishes between 'rationality' (acting on the best critical discussion) and 'logical probability' (induction); by collapsing the preference into mere psychology, the target falsely attributes to Popper an irrationalist stance he explicitly rejected in favor of a non-inductive rationality.
